stem: Seven-year-old Lotta has vomiting, anorexia, low-grade fever, and right lower quadrant pain that started peri-umbilically. To support the clinical diagnosis of appendicitis, which of the following findings is LEAST likely to be encountered?

options.text: Enlarged/ thickened appendix vermicularis on abdominal ultrasound.
No visualisation of the appendix vermicularis on abdominal ultrasound.

explanation: Appendicitis commonly causes leukocytosis with neutrophilia and ultrasound may show an enlarged, thickened appendix or non-visualisation of the appendix. Anaemia is not a typical acute finding in appendicitis and is therefore the least likely result.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

optionExplanations.C: Not a usual acute feature of appendicitis.
optionExplanations.D: A classic ultrasound finding in appendicitis.
optionExplanations.E: The appendix is sometimes not seen on ultrasound, especially in children.
